# Engine v13.3 release notes, mined while the arcs are fresh

Terminal predicate: Engine 13.3's release note, `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.3.0.md`, tells what 13.3 shipped to the release-notes bar, passes the §7 cut-readiness checklist at the cut head, and the 13.3 cut (#19652) publishes it.

## Problem

13.3 is the first Engine release on the one-to-two-week cadence the ROADMAP set after 13.2 ("Next: Engine 13.3 — The Grid Fits Its Content"). Milestone v13.3 is due 2026-10-25. Its cut record #19652 authors the note "through the release-notes epic" and keeps the notes out of its own scope, but that epic does not exist. Without the file, `publish.mjs prepare` stops on `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.3.0.md is missing` (`buildScripts/release/releaseState.mjs:90`).

The arcs are cheapest to mine now, while their sessions are fresh; `#14800` was seeded on that lesson. Since 13.2.0 (published 2026-10-11T22:37Z), GitHub search counted 34 merged PRs in neo, 11 in neo-stage, 6 in Brain and 0 in Institution at 2026-10-13T14:02Z. These are search counts; the note's scope comes from the corpus script at the cut (§2).

The bar now includes pictures. The operator's verdict on a 13.2 draft asked for a narrative that focuses on what matters, and for screenshots ([#14800 comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14800#issuecomment-6080548526)); the final 13.2.0 note carries nine images. 13.3's release gate is behaviour you can see.

## Why an epic

The release-notes workflow (§1) makes notes an epic by design: an early iteration-1 draft under a status banner, mining-driven refinement leaves, and a final cut-readiness iteration. Each is a one-PR leaf with its own cross-family review.

## Intended solution

- **The three cornerstones lead,** each mined before it is drafted (§3): content-sized rows (#19658, closed; steward Ada), grid header menus (#19643; steward Vega) and a cut the maintainers can run (#19637; steward Grace). The steward who lived an arc mines it cheapest, so each deposits one mining comment here once the arc has landed: session ids, PR chain, timeline, numbers.
- **Screenshots of what the gate names:** the 10k wrapped-text grid holding its rows through scrolling, and a header menu filtering by checked values with live counts.
- **Also in 13.3,** taken from the §2 scope run rather than memory. Known candidates: the Brain-gated e2e tier on every Engine PR (#19657, after the `dev`-push burn-in of #19656) and the Portal's featured Workstation reaching the package (#19640).
- **Honest bounds:** e2e-proven behaviour stays apart from bounded witnesses, such as the header menu's 100k timing.
- Iteration 1 merges early under the banner; the last iteration regenerates scope at the cut head and removes it.

## Out of scope

- The cut mechanics and the version bump (#19652).
- What 13.3 contains: milestone v13.3 and the ROADMAP decide that.
- Blog posts (#13383).
- Brain and Institution notes, which belong to their own release lines.

## Avoided traps

- **Writing the plan instead of the release.** A cornerstone that misses the window moves to 13.4 (ROADMAP, "How it runs"), so the note describes what merged by the cut head. Cornerstone 2's last leaf (#19671, in review as #19711) is the live case.
- **Shrinking the release** ("just a grid release"): §1 rule 4.
- **A leaf that bundles drafting with cut mechanics.**

Related: #19652 (the cut) · #14800 (13.2's notes) · ROADMAP "Next: Engine 13.3" · `.agents/skills/release-notes/`
